property_summary: For any inputs to initialize(...), the correct C sets its baseToken state to the provided _baseToken parameter (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialize succeeds); the mutant unconditionally sets baseToken to address(0) and thus will differ for any _baseToken != address(0).

For all calls to initialize(...), the contract's public baseToken equals the _baseToken argument passed (reference preserves the parameter), whereas the mutant assigns baseToken = msg.sender and thus for some inputs baseToken != _baseToken.

For any initialize(...) call that succeeds, the reference implementation always sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken before returning; the mutant that delays assigning baseToken until after setting initialized can leave baseToken as the zero-address in some scenarios (e.g., if initialization's effects are observed/interleaved), so there exist inputs where the mutant's baseToken != _baseToken while the reference's equals _baseToken.

After a successful initialize(...) call, baseToken must equal the _baseToken argument; the mutant that sets initialized before assigning baseToken can result in baseToken == address(0) (not equal to the provided _baseToken) for some inputs when the call appears to succeed, so the rule is violated by that mutant.

For every call to initialize(...) that returns (does not revert), the reference contract sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken; the mutant (which sets initialized = true before assigning baseToken) can return while leaving baseToken as address(0) for some fuzzed inputs, so there exists an input where the mutant's baseToken != the provided argument while the reference's equals it.

For any call to initialize(...) that returns (does not revert), the reference contract always sets baseToken == the supplied _baseToken; the mutant (which sets initialized = true before assigning baseToken) can return while leaving baseToken == address(0) for some fuzzed inputs, so there exists inputs where the mutant's stored baseToken differs from the provided argument.

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract always sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken before returning; the mutant (which sets initialized = true before assigning baseToken) can enable a reentrant call that observes initialized==true and calls initialize again (or otherwise exploit reentrancy) causing baseToken to remain address(0) while the reference would have set it—so there exist fuzzed inputs (a reentrant caller target address) that make the mutant leave baseToken != provided _baseToken while the reference preserves equality.

For any _baseToken passed to initialize, the correct contract sets c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialization; the mutant erroneously sets baseToken to the factory address so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken.

For any inputs to initialize, a successful initialize call must set nft to the provided _nft before marking initialized (so after a successful call c.nft() == _nft); the mutant that assigns nft after setting initialized can cause a different nft (or zero) observable after initialize for some inputs (e.g. when external interactions depend on nft during initialization), so there exists inputs where the mutant's nft() != _nft while the reference always sets nft==_nft on success.

After any successful initialize(...) call, the contract's nft() getter must equal the _nft argument; the mutant that assigns nft after setting initialized can cause nft() to differ for some inputs when an external call during initialize (e.g. the emitted Initialize event delivery to an address with a reverting fallback) causes control-flow to observe/affect nft assignment, so the mutant violates nft()==_nft for some fuzzed inputs.

For any inputs where initialize(...) returns normally, the reference contract always sets nft() equal to the _nft argument; the mutant that assigns nft after setting initialized can have initialize return normally but leave nft() different (or zero) for some inputs when a reentrant/failing external interaction during initialize affects control flow — so there exists fuzzed inputs (a specially crafted _nft address that is a contract with a reverting fallback) where the mutant's nft() != the provided _nft while the reference always preserves nft()==_nft.

For any call to initialize(...) that returns normally, the reference contract always sets nft() equal to the _nft argument; the mutant (which assigns nft after other state and after setting initialized) can be made to return normally while leaving nft() different by using an adversarial _nft contract that reverts on certain interactions during initialize, causing observable divergence.

For every call to initialize(...) that returns normally, the reference sets nft() == _nft; the mutant (which assigns nft after other state and after setting initialized) can be forced by making the factory.ownerOf(...) call revert during initialize to return normally but leave nft different, so nft() != _nft for some adversarial _nft addresses.

For any initialize(...) call the contract's public nft() getter returns the same address that was passed in as the _nft parameter; the mutant sets nft to address(0) instead and thus violates this for inputs where _nft != address(0).

After initialize(...) completes successfully, the contract's public nft() getter always equals the _nft argument passed to initialize; the mutant that deletes the assignment to nft breaks this by leaving nft unchanged for some inputs.
For any inputs to initialize, the contract's stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument provided; the mutant that sets changeFee = 0 breaks this rule for inputs where _changeFee != 0.

For any initialize(...) inputs, the contract stores changeFee equal to the provided _changeFee (i.e., c.changeFee() == _changeFee); the mutant that doubles the assignment breaks this by making c.changeFee() == _changeFee * 2 for some inputs.

For any initialize(...) call the contract's stored changeFee equals the input _changeFee (reference), but the mutant increments it by 1, so there exist inputs where c.changeFee() != _changeFee (the mutant breaks this equality).

For any input to initialize where _feeRate is within the allowed maximum (<=5000), the contract stores feeRate exactly equal to the provided _feeRate; the mutant caps the stored feeRate to at most 1000, violating this when _feeRate > 1000 and <=5000.

For any feeRate value less than or equal to 5000, calling initialize on a fresh C should succeed and set initialized==true; the mutant that changes the check to >=5000 will incorrectly reject feeRate == 5000 causing initialized to remain false for that input.

For any input to initialize, the reference contract always sets initialized to true after a successful call; the mutant that omits setting initialized leaves initialized == false for some inputs, so initialized() must be true after initialize(...) in the correct contract but can be false in the buggy one.
